summary: AgriSeva is a farmer-first agricultural decision-support web portal developed by Team AntarikshYaan (Milan Javoor, Dewang Sharma, Pranav Bharadwaj) for the 2026 NASA Space Apps Challenge. Facing shifting temperatures, erratic rainfall, groundwater depletion, and declining soil health, farmers need practical tools to evaluate multi-season crop rotations. AgriSeva allows users to select any farm location via an interactive map or coordinates, specify local soil properties and baseline rotations, and weight priorities such as water conservation, nitrogen fixation, pest disruption, and market suitability. Powered by live NASA POWER agroclimatology data alongside a harmonized multi-sensor catalog (SMAP, GPM IMERG, ECOSTRESS, SRTM, Landsat/MODIS, GEDI, USDA SSURGO, FAO GAEZ, and OpenET), AgriSeva compares three adaptive rotation paths side-by-side—highlighting supporting climate evidence, quantified agronomic benefits, and field-level risks requiring verification with local agronomists.
details:
What It Does & How It Works: AgriSeva bridges the gap between orbital Earth-observation datasets and day-to-day farm rotation decisions without requiring GIS expertise. Farmers select their field on an interactive Leaflet/OpenStreetMap interface (demonstrated on the Punjab grain belt at 30.7333° N, 76.7794° E), choose their soil class (Alluvial, Vertisol, Alfisol, Sandy Loam), enter their current rotation (e.g., Rice–Wheat), and prioritize goals (water conservation, biological nitrogen fixation, pest-cycle disruption, or market fit).

Four-Stage Data & Modeling Pipeline:

  1. Orbital Signals: Fetches live NASA POWER monthly climatology (corrected precipitation, 2 m air temperature, surface solar irradiance, and 2 m wind speed) integrated with multi-sensor context from SMAP (soil moisture), GPM IMERG (rainfall extremes), ECOSTRESS (heat & evapotranspiration), SRTM (elevation/runoff), Landsat/MODIS/NAIP (NDVI), and GEDI (biomass).
  2. Ground & Market Layers: Incorporates USDA NRCS SSURGO/STATSGO2 soil attributes, USDA CropScape, USGS NLCD, PRISM, USGS NWIS, FAO GAEZ crop suitability, OpenET, and USDA AMS Market News.
  3. 10 km Spatial Harmonization & Multi-Criteria Scoring: Aligns multi-resolution environmental indicators onto a common analysis grid to detect dry windows, bare-soil exposure, and water deficits.
  4. Explainable Three-Path Comparison: Evaluates the farmer's current baseline (e.g., Rice–Wheat: 0% water saved, 0 kg/ha N fixed) against a Climate-Resilient path (Millet + Pulse Intercrop → Chickpea: 28% water saved, 42 kg/ha N fixed, 68/100 market fit) and a Soil-Building path (Legume Cover → Sorghum → Pulse: 19% water saved, 58 kg/ha N fixed, 5/5 pest-cycle break).

Scientific Transparency & Human-in-the-Loop Safeguards: AgriSeva explicitly distinguishes live NASA POWER telemetry from catalogued contextual datasets, flags grid-scale microclimate uncertainties, and provides tailored "Verify Locally" checklists so farmers validate seed, soil, and buyer conditions with local extension officers.

Tools & Technologies Used: React / TypeScript / Tailwind CSS (built via Emergent), Leaflet.js & OpenStreetMap, NASA POWER Agroclimatology REST API, and Python/HTML data-visualization workflows.
